title: Dead-letter queue (DLQ) + operator replay tooling for audit export batches
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — SIEM-ready audit export (Beta)
description:
We need a DLQ mechanism and safe replay tooling for the audit-log-exporter so that permanent / repeated destination failures (auth, invalid config, schema issues, sustained throttling) do not cause unbounded retries, data loss, or operator guesswork. DLQ must preserve enough context to replay deterministically while respecting privacy/redaction rules. Provide operator controls to replay with guardrails to avoid data duplication storms (at-least-once system; downstream dedup required).

Scope:
- DLQ sink for failed batches per destination adapter, with reason codes, attempt counts, timestamps, and minimal replay payload.
- Replay tooling (CLI) for operators (SRE / on-call) to list DLQ items, inspect, and replay selectively.
- Safety controls: per-tenant and per-destination replay rate limiting, max batch size, exponential backoff on replay, replay dry-run/validate mode, and hard safety stop when exporter lag is above threshold.
- Observability: metrics for DLQ depth/age, replay attempts/success/failure, and alert hooks.

Non-goals:
- Exactly-once delivery. We remain at-least-once; replay may produce duplicates. Our responsibility is to minimize duplicates via idempotency keys and to provide explicit operator warnings + throttles.

References:
- ADR (delivery semantics/idempotency): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-audit-export-delivery-semantics-and-idempotency.json
- Service architecture: sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/audit-exporter-service-architecture.json
- SRE SLOs/alerting: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/audit-exporter-slos-and-alerting.json
acceptance_criteria: When a batch exceeds retry budget or hits a non-retryable error, it is written to DLQ with tenant_id, destination_id, adapter, failure_reason, first_seen_at, last_attempt_at, attempt_count, and a replay pointer (not raw unredacted payloads).

Replay CLI supports: list --tenant <id> [--destination <id>] [--since <ts>], show <dlq_id>, replay <dlq_id> [--max-qps N] [--max-bytes N] [--dry-run] [--confirm], and replay-bulk with explicit filters + confirmation.
Replay tooling enforces guardrails: default low QPS, per-tenant concurrency limit, and refuses bulk replay unless operator provides explicit --confirm and a bounded window/filter.
Replay emits metrics + logs with correlation IDs and links to original failure reason; DLQ depth and replay success rate are visible on dashboards.
Runbook updates: how to use replay tooling, when NOT to replay (e.g., destination misconfigured), and customer comms guidance.
Security review: DLQ contents do not introduce new PII leakage; respects audit event redaction policy; secrets never logged.
design_notes:
Proposed model (implemented):
- DLQ unit = "failed export batch" (not individual event), keyed by dlq_id.
- DLQ record stores a replay_pointer referencing persisted batch object (already encrypted at rest) OR reconstructable fetch cursor + destination config version. For S3 adapter, pointer = (tenant_id, destination_id, checkpoint_range, object_key prefix). For HTTP adapters (Splunk/Datadog), pointer = internal batch blob key (encrypted) produced pre-send.
- Reason codes normalized across adapters: AUTH_INVALID, DESTINATION_REJECTED_4XX, RATE_LIMITED_EXHAUSTED, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED, CONFIG_INVALID, NETWORK_EXHAUSTED, UNKNOWN.

Guardrails:
- Token bucket per (tenant_id, destination_id) for replays; defaults: 1 batch/sec, burst 3.
- Hard cap on replay batch size (bytes) and event count; refuse replay if cap exceeded unless operator uses --override-cap with ticket reference.
- Replay uses the same idempotency strategy as live delivery (event_id per event). We do not attempt to de-dup within exporter beyond per-batch idempotency headers where supported; we rely on downstream dedup guidance.
- Safety stop: if exporter lag metric > max_lag_safety_threshold (from config), replay is blocked by default to avoid amplifying backlog; override requires --force and emits audit log event.

Operationally:
- Replay actions themselves produce Redwood audit events (who replayed what, when, filters used), but replay does not re-emit original business audit events; it only re-sends already-generated batches.
implementation_plan:
1) Add DLQ interface + implementation (cloud-managed queue/store) and adapter hooks for "give up" paths.
2) Extend retry policy to classify retryable vs non-retryable errors and define retry budget per adapter.
3) Add operator CLI (internal) with authN/authZ, bounded queries, and explicit confirmation UX.
4) Instrumentation + dashboards panels for DLQ/replay.
5) Update runbook and on-call training.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Duplication storms during replay (downstream sees same events many times).
- Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-tenant rate limits, bounded bulk replay, mandatory confirmations, block replay when lag high, and strong operator warnings.

Risk: DLQ becomes a shadow data lake (retention + PII).
- Mitigation: store pointers + minimal metadata; encrypt at rest; TTL on DLQ metadata; ensure batch blobs inherit existing retention policies; validate redaction.

Risk: Operators replay with wrong destination config (e.g., after rotation) causing repeated failures.
- Mitigation: dlq show displays destination config version/hash; replay validates destination health/test-connection status; recommended to fix config before replay.
comments: 2025-02-05 — Rafael Mendes: We had two separate beta risks called out in SRE review: (1) unbounded retries during downstream 429s; (2) no safe replay path when we intentionally stop retrying. This ticket covers (2). Please coordinate with Sean on guardrails and with Marcus on what is acceptable to store in DLQ. Priority P0 for beta readiness.

2025-02-07 — Aisha Bello: Drafted DLQ record format + reason codes. Key decision: DLQ should store a pointer to an encrypted batch blob (already produced for sending) rather than duplicating raw events. This reduces PII exposure and avoids schema drift. Will post PR plan to #eng-sre once CLI UX is clearer.

2025-02-10 — Marcus Lin: +1 on pointer-only; ensure DLQ metadata doesn’t include request headers (user agents) or destination auth details. Replay CLI must never print payloads by default. If we add a "show" command, it should show only metadata + counts; payload inspection should be a separate break-glass flow (out of scope).

2025-02-13 — Sean Gallagher: Guardrails request: replay must be disabled by default when lag is already elevated. Also need a cap on concurrency per tenant; a single noisy customer shouldn’t starve exporter workers during replay. Add metrics for DLQ age (oldest item) and replay outcome.

2025-02-18 — Aisha Bello: Implementing replay CLI with explicit confirmation gates:
- replay-bulk requires both a bounded filter (since/until OR max-items) and --confirm.
- default max-qps=1; max-items=100 unless overridden.
- replay action emits an audit event (operator, tenant, dlq_ids). Ethan’s team confirmed we can reuse internal operator identity plumbing.

Open question: TTL for DLQ metadata. Proposal: 14 days in beta; align with backfill window defaults.

2025-02-21 — Kevin Osei: TTL=14d is OK for beta as long as the policy doc does not imply guaranteed availability of DLQ items. Make it explicit: DLQ is an operational buffer, not a customer-facing retention mechanism.

2025-02-27 — Aisha Bello: PR up with DLQ + replay CLI, including per-tenant rate limit + size caps. Still need to wire dashboard panels in ENG-5168, but metrics names are in place. Requesting review from Logan (metrics) and Marcus (security).

2025-03-03 — Logan Wright: Metrics naming looks aligned. Please keep labels low-cardinality: tenant_id should be hashed or omitted from Prometheus; destination_id can explode cardinality too. Recommend: export_adapter, error_reason, and a small enum for destination_type. For troubleshooting tenant-specific issues, rely on logs/traces with sampling.

2025-03-05 — Aisha Bello: Updated metrics per Logan guidance: removed tenant_id label; added destination_type + adapter + reason. Replay CLI now prints a warning explaining at-least-once semantics + potential duplicates, and requires --confirm for anything > 10 items.

2025-03-07 — Sean Gallagher: Ran through the tool during on-call training. Biggest missing piece was a safety stop when lag is high; we can ship without it if replay defaults are conservative, but I’d prefer follow-up in backpressure ticket. Adding explicit runbook steps: fix destination creds first, then replay limited window, then monitor lag + DLQ depth.

2025-03-14 — Aisha Bello: Merged PR-1093. Follow-up items tracked separately: (a) lag safety stop + auto-pausing is in PR-1119; (b) dashboard panels/alerts in ENG-5168. Marking this ticket Done for beta scope.
